sam: Quick thread — canary favors us-east-1 ~85% even with client-region hints. I think edge affinity TTL is too long for these workloads; proposing default 30s + explicit rollback header emitted by console.
anya: 30s could be fine for latency-sensitive endpoints, but that will ups backend cold starts. Do we want header-only rollback or a control-plane signal too?
maria: Header approach is less invasive. We can have Console flip a canary flag and set header like `X-Redwood-Rollback: canary-2024-11` for in-flight traffic. Router treats that as higher precedence than geo-hint.
kevin: Agree on header precedence. We also need telemetry slices: `routing.affinity_hits`, `routing.rollback_signals`, and tag by tenant + region. Otherwise postmortems are messy.
sam: Proposed header format for router to parse:
```
X-Redwood-Routing: affinity=edge;affinity-ttl=30;rollback=canary-2024-11
```
maria: Can we make TTL configurable per-tenant? Some enterprise customers want longer affinity for compliance reasons.
anya: Yes, tenant override makes sense. UX idea: Console shows slider for "Edge affinity TTL" with an estimated RPS and cost delta preview.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created canary flag `canary-2024-11` for svc/api-gw, rollout 5% -> 25% over 30m :rocket:
kevin: One more: ensure rollback header wins over fallback policies. Also log `route.origin` and `route.decider` in traces so we know whether header or geo-policy chose the region.
